question: What still requires excessive ChatGPT reasoning/tool orchestration after reusable workflows can compose?

proposals.title: Structured transactional / AST editing
proposals.evidence: Gen4 reduced normal lifecycle top-level sequencing from 4 to 1 calls (75%), but the real edit-heavy authoring proxy only fell from 4591B to 4449B (3.1%). The remaining payload was dominated by exact old/new source text rather than orchestration.
proposals.expected_benefit: Replace large exact-string edit payloads with audited symbol/AST/structured transformations, deterministic preconditions, previews, rollback, and provenance.

proposals.title: Automatic composite/skill synthesis from successful traces
proposals.evidence: Registered graphs can now be reused with zero newly authored procedural steps and combined lifecycle calls fell 7 to 2, but accepted composites are still designed and registered manually.
proposals.expected_benefit: Mine repeated successful workflow sequences and propose bounded immutable composites requiring explicit acceptance.

proposals.title: Adaptive bounded recovery policies
proposals.evidence: Recovery succeeds with bounded retries, but graph recovery branches remain static and hand-authored.
proposals.expected_benefit: Select among a declared bounded set of inspect/retry/rollback actions using explicit budgets and state predicates.

proposals.title: Static analysis + property fuzzing for workflows and graphs
proposals.evidence: Gen4 enlarged the graph/schema surface beyond example-based tests despite typed mappings, cycles, bounds and restart checkpoints.
proposals.expected_benefit: Generate bounded malformed definitions, mappings, restart fixtures and interruption states to prove fail-closed behavior.

proposals.title: Parallel execution of independent DAG nodes
proposals.evidence: The accepted DAG runner executes independent topological nodes sequentially; concurrency was intentionally deferred because wall-clock was not Gen4's objective.
proposals.expected_benefit: Run dependency-independent resource-compatible children concurrently with explicit fan-out and deterministic join/failure semantics.
